answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock scarce tokens before bidding, with rewards and penalties settled after audited tasks. Influence grows only as stake survives work over a long horizon; splitting funds among fresh identities dilutes each one's weight. A mirror of this rule is that honest agents also risk losses, so audits need appeal. A lotus name or new key cannot remove the attacker's cost: capital remains locked and slashable across attempts.
